subQuestions.label: 1(a)(1)
subQuestions.questionText:
Given $17\sin\theta - 15 = 0$ and $\theta \in [90°; 270°]$. $P(x; 15)$ lies on the terminal ray of $\theta$, at a distance of 17 from the origin.

Without a calculator, determine the value of $\tan(180° + \theta)$.
subQuestions.memoText:
$\sin\theta = \dfrac{15}{17}$; with $\theta$ in Quadrant 2 and $x^2 + 15^2 = 17^2$, $x = -8$.
$\tan(180° + \theta) = \tan\theta = \dfrac{15}{-8} = -\dfrac{15}{8}$

subQuestions.label: 1(a)(2)
subQuestions.questionText: Without a calculator, determine the value of $\cos(90° + \theta)$.
subQuestions.memoText: $\cos(90° + \theta) = -\sin\theta = -\dfrac{15}{17}$

subQuestions.label: 1(b)
subQuestions.questionText: Use a calculator to solve for $\theta$.

subQuestions.label: 2(a)(1)
subQuestions.questionText: Showing all working, without the use of a calculator, determine the value of $\tan 300°$.

subQuestions.label: 2(a)(2)
subQuestions.questionText: Showing all working, without a calculator, determine the value of $\cos^2 15° - \sin^2 15°$.

subQuestions.label: 2(b)
subQuestions.questionText: Determine the general solution(s) for $4\cos(2\theta + 60°) = -2$.
subQuestions.memoText:
$\cos(2\theta + 60°) = -\dfrac{1}{2}$; reference angle $120°$.
$2\theta + 60° = \pm 120° + k\cdot 360°$, $k \in \mathbb{Z}$
$2\theta = 60° + k\cdot 360°$  or  $2\theta = -180° + k\cdot 360°$
$\theta = 30° + k\cdot 180°$  or  $\theta = -90° + k\cdot 180°$, $k \in \mathbb{Z}$

subQuestions.label: 3(a)(1)
subQuestions.questionText:
The marks (as whole percentages) of 15 learners for their Grade 11 November Mathematics examinations are shown in a scatter plot (Paper 1 on the horizontal axis, Paper 2 on the vertical axis).

State the mark for Paper 1 of the learner who did the best.

subQuestions.label: 3(a)(2)
subQuestions.questionText: State the lowest mark for Paper 2.

subQuestions.label: 3(a)(3)(i)
subQuestions.questionText: The line of best fit has the equation $y = 5{,}862 + 0{,}8541x$. If a learner got 67% for Paper 1, what could that learner expect to get for Paper 2? Round your answer to the nearest whole.

subQuestions.label: 3(a)(3)(ii)
subQuestions.questionText: If it is further given that the mean for Paper 1 ($\bar{x}$) was 67%, sketch the line of best fit on the scatter plot above, clearly indicating the $y$-intercept and the point $(\bar{x}; \bar{y})$.
subQuestions.memoText:
$y$-intercept: $(0; 5{,}862)$; $(\bar{x}; \bar{y}) = (67; 63{,}09)$. Draw the line through both points.
Marks: $y$-intercept; $(\bar{x}; \bar{y})$; line.

subQuestions.label: 3(b)
subQuestions.questionText:
A survey of 140 people was done to see how many WhatsApp messages they sent in a day. Complete the table of results and plot the ogive on the grid.

| Number of messages | Frequency | Cumulative frequency |
| $20 < x \leq 40$ | ? | 14 |
| $40 < x \leq 60$ | 32 | ? |
| $60 < x \leq 80$ | 54 | ? |
| $80 < x \leq 100$ | 27 | ? |
| $100 < x \leq 120$ | ? | 140 |
subQuestions.memoText:
Frequencies: $14$, $32$, $54$, $27$, $13$.
Cumulative frequencies: $14$, $46$, $100$, $127$, $140$.
Plot the ogive with start point $(20; 0)$ and end point $(120; 140)$; join with a smooth curve.

subQuestions.label: 4(a)
subQuestions.questionText:
Sketched are the graphs $f(x) = a\cos x$ and $g(x) = \sin bx$ where $x \in [0°; 210°]$.

State the amplitude of $f$.

subQuestions.label: 4(b)
subQuestions.questionText: State the period of $g$.

subQuestions.label: 4(c)(1)
subQuestions.questionText: Write down the coordinates of A, the turning point of $g$.

subQuestions.label: 4(c)(2)
subQuestions.questionText: Write down the coordinates of B, the point of intersection of $f$ and $g$.
subQuestions.memoText: $B\left(210°; \dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right)$

subQuestions.label: 4(d)
subQuestions.questionText: If $x \in [0°; 210°]$, determine the value(s) of $x$ where $g(x) \leq 0$.

subQuestions.label: 5(a)
subQuestions.questionText: On the axes below, sketch the graph of $h(x) = -\tan x$ where $x \in [-180°; 180°]$.
subQuestions.memoText:
Reflected tangent curve. Vertical asymptotes at $x = -90°$ and $x = 90°$; passes through $(-180°; 0)$, $(0; 0)$ and $(180°; 0)$; decreasing between consecutive asymptotes.
Marks: asymptotes; shape; accuracy.

subQuestions.label: 5(b)
subQuestions.questionText: If $h(x)$ is shifted up two units, write the equation of the new graph in the form $y = \ldots$
subQuestions.memoText: $y = -\tan x + 2$

subQuestions.label: 5(c)
subQuestions.questionText: If $k(x) = -\tan(x - p)$, give the value of $p$ if the asymptotes of $k(x)$ are $x = -135°$ and $x = 45°$.
subQuestions.memoText:
$-\tan x$ has asymptotes at $x = \pm 90°$; shifting by $p$ gives asymptotes at $x = \pm 90° + p$.
$45° = 90° + p \Rightarrow p = -45°$ (and $-135° = -90° + p$ gives the same).
$\therefore p = -45°$

questions.title: Analytical Geometry — Inclination, Perpendicular Bisector & Parallelogram

subQuestions.label: 6(a)
subQuestions.questionText:
$\triangle$ABC has vertices $A(-2; 4)$, $B(6; p)$ and $C(3; -3)$. BC has an angle of inclination of $59{,}0362°$.

Find the gradient of AC.

subQuestions.label: 6(b)
subQuestions.questionText: Find $\theta$ (the angle of inclination of AC) and hence determine the size of angle $\hat{C}$.
subQuestions.memoText:
$\tan\theta = -\dfrac{7}{5} \Rightarrow \theta = -54{,}46° + 180° = 125{,}54°$.
$\hat{C} = 125{,}54° - 59{,}0362° = 66{,}51°$ (exterior angle of $\triangle$ / angle between the two lines).

subQuestions.label: 6(c)
subQuestions.questionText: Determine M, the midpoint of line AC.
subQuestions.memoText: $M = \left(\dfrac{-2 + 3}{2}; \dfrac{4 + (-3)}{2}\right) = \left(\dfrac{1}{2}; \dfrac{1}{2}\right)$

subQuestions.label: 6(d)
subQuestions.questionText: Determine the equation of the line perpendicular to AC passing through the midpoint of AC (the perpendicular bisector of AC). Leave your answer in the form $y = mx + c$.
subQuestions.memoText:
$m_\perp = \dfrac{5}{7}$
$y - \dfrac{1}{2} = \dfrac{5}{7}\left(x - \dfrac{1}{2}\right)$
$y = \dfrac{5}{7}x - \dfrac{5}{14} + \dfrac{1}{2} = \dfrac{5}{7}x + \dfrac{1}{7}$

subQuestions.label: 6(e)
subQuestions.questionText: Showing all working, determine the value of $p$.

subQuestions.label: 6(f)
subQuestions.questionText: If the value of $p$ is 2, determine D, the fourth point of the parallelogram ABCD. D lies in the third quadrant.
subQuestions.memoText:
For ABCD a parallelogram, the diagonals AC and BD bisect: midpoint AC $= \left(\dfrac{1}{2}; \dfrac{1}{2}\right)$ = midpoint BD.
$\left(\dfrac{x + 6}{2}; \dfrac{y + 2}{2}\right) = \left(\dfrac{1}{2}; \dfrac{1}{2}\right) \Rightarrow x = -5$, $y = -1$.
$D(-5; -1)$

questions.title: Circle Geometry — Cyclic Quadrilateral Proof; Cosine & Sine Rules

subQuestions.label: 7(a)
subQuestions.questionText:
Use the diagram below to prove the statement that says: 'The opposite angles of a cyclic quadrilateral are supplementary.'

Required to prove: $\hat{A} + \hat{C} = 180°$.
subQuestions.memoText:
Construction: draw radii OB and OD.
Let $\hat{A} = x$.
$\hat{O}_2 = 2x$ (angle at centre $= 2 \times$ angle at circle, subtended by BD).
$\hat{O}_1 = 360° - 2x$ (angles around a point).
$\hat{C} = \dfrac{1}{2}\hat{O}_1 = 180° - x$ (angle at centre $= 2 \times$ angle at circle).
$\therefore \hat{A} + \hat{C} = x + (180° - x) = 180°$.

subQuestions.label: 7(b)(1)
subQuestions.questionText:
Given cyclic quadrilateral EFGH with $\hat{G} = 114°$, EF = 12 units, FG = 8 units and GH = 6 units.

Determine the length of FH. State all relevant reasons with your statements.
subQuestions.memoText:
In $\triangle$FGH (cosine rule):
$FH^2 = (8)^2 + (6)^2 - 2(8)(6)\cos 114°$
$FH = 11{,}79$ units

subQuestions.label: 7(b)(2)
subQuestions.questionText: Determine the size of $\hat{H}_2$, if $\hat{H}_2$ is an acute angle.
subQuestions.memoText:
$\hat{E} = 180° - 114° = 66°$ (opposite angles of cyclic quadrilateral EFGH).
In $\triangle$EFH (sine rule): $\dfrac{\sin\hat{H}_2}{12} = \dfrac{\sin 66°}{11{,}79}$
$\sin\hat{H}_2 = 0{,}9298\ldots$
$\hat{H}_2 = 68{,}41°$

questions.title: Circle Geometry — Parallel Chords & the Diameter

subQuestions.label: 8(a)(1)
subQuestions.questionText:
Given the circle with cyclic points J, K, L and M, where HL // JK and $LH \perp KM$. LM = 15 units and MH = 12 units.

Give the reason for the statement: $\hat{K} = 90°$.
subQuestions.memoText: Alternate angles, HL // JK (so $\hat{K} = \hat{H}_1 = 90°$, since $LH \perp KM$).

subQuestions.label: 8(a)(2)
subQuestions.questionText: Give the reason for the statement: $\hat{L}_1 + \hat{L}_2 = 90°$.
subQuestions.memoText: Angles in the same segment (subtending the same chord KM as $\hat{K} = 90°$).

subQuestions.label: 8(b)
subQuestions.questionText: Determine the length of GH.
subQuestions.memoText:
In right-angled $\triangle$LMG (right angle at L), LH is the altitude to the hypotenuse MG:
$LM^2 = MH \times MG$ (perpendicular from the right-angled vertex)
$15^2 = 12 \times MG \Rightarrow MG = 18{,}75$
$GH = MG - MH = 18{,}75 - 12 = 6{,}75$ units

subQuestions.label: 8(c)
subQuestions.questionText: Give a reason why LM is the diameter of the circle passing through LHM.
subQuestions.memoText: Converse of the angle in a semi-circle: $\hat{H} = 90°$, so LM subtends a right angle and is therefore a diameter.

subQuestions.label: 9(a)
subQuestions.questionText:
Prove:

$$\dfrac{\cos 65x\cos 63x + \sin 65x\sin 63x}{1 + \sin 2x} = \dfrac{\cos x - \sin x}{\cos x + \sin x}$$
subQuestions.memoText:
Numerator $= \cos(65x - 63x) = \cos 2x = \cos^2 x - \sin^2 x = (\cos x + \sin x)(\cos x - \sin x)$.
Denominator $= 1 + \sin 2x = \cos^2 x + \sin^2 x + 2\sin x\cos x = (\cos x + \sin x)^2$.
LHS $= \dfrac{(\cos x + \sin x)(\cos x - \sin x)}{(\cos x + \sin x)^2} = \dfrac{\cos x - \sin x}{\cos x + \sin x}$ = RHS.

subQuestions.label: 9(b)
subQuestions.questionText: Determine the values of $x$ where $\dfrac{\cos 65x\cos 63x + \sin 65x\sin 63x}{1 + \sin 2x}$ is undefined, if $x \in [-90°; 180°]$.
subQuestions.memoText:
Undefined where the denominator $1 + \sin 2x = 0$, i.e. $\sin 2x = -1$.
Reference angle $-90°$: $2x = -90° + k\cdot 360°$, so $x = -45° + k\cdot 180°$, $k \in \mathbb{Z}$.
In $[-90°; 180°]$: $x = -45°$ or $x = 135°$.

subQuestions.label: 10(a)
subQuestions.questionText:
A survey recorded the community service hours already completed by a Grade 12 group:

| Hours completed | Frequency |
| $0 \leq h < 6$ | 5 |
| $6 \leq h < 12$ | $p$ |
| $12 \leq h < 18$ | 28 |
| $18 \leq h \leq 24$ | 4 |

The estimated average number of hours was 12. By using the table, determine how many learners completed less than this average.
subQuestions.memoText:
Midpoints: $3$, $9$, $15$, $21$.
$12 = \dfrac{(5)(3) + (p)(9) + (28)(15) + (4)(21)}{37 + p} = \dfrac{519 + 9p}{37 + p}$
$12(37 + p) = 519 + 9p \Rightarrow 444 + 12p = 519 + 9p \Rightarrow 3p = 75 \Rightarrow p = 25$
Learners completing less than 12 hours $= 5 + 25 = 30$ learners.

subQuestions.label: 10(b)(1)
subQuestions.questionText:
A set of data has $\sigma = 2$ and $\displaystyle\sum_{i=1}^{n}(x_i - \mu)^2 = 32$.

How many data values were used in this set of data?
subQuestions.memoText:
$\sigma^2 = \dfrac{\sum(x_i - \mu)^2}{n}$
$2^2 = \dfrac{32}{n}$
$n = 8$

subQuestions.label: 10(b)(2)
subQuestions.questionText: 10 new identical values are added to the data set; as a result, the mean remains the same. Determine the new standard deviation.
subQuestions.memoText:
Each new value equals the mean, so it contributes $0$ to $\sum(x_i - \mu)^2$, which stays at $32$.
New $n = 8 + 10 = 18$.
$\sigma^2 = \dfrac{32}{18} \Rightarrow \sigma = 1{,}33$

subQuestions.label: 11(a)
subQuestions.questionText:
A circle has centre C. $\triangle$ADE is drawn with $D(-4; -1)$ and $E(8; 3)$, and AB = BD. $F(0; 6)$ is the $y$-cut of line BC.

Prove BC // DE.
subQuestions.memoText:
AB = BD (given, so B is the midpoint of AD) and AC = CE (radii — A and E lie on the circle with centre C).
$\therefore$ BC // DE (midpoint theorem).

subQuestions.label: 11(b)
subQuestions.questionText: Find the length of BC.
subQuestions.memoText:
$DE = \sqrt{(-4 - 8)^2 + (-1 - 3)^2} = \sqrt{144 + 16} = \sqrt{160} = 4\sqrt{10}$.
$BC = \dfrac{1}{2}DE = 2\sqrt{10}$ (midpoint theorem).

subQuestions.label: 11(c)
subQuestions.questionText: If the equation of line AE is $y = -\dfrac{4}{5}x + \dfrac{47}{5}$, determine the equation of the circle.
subQuestions.memoText:
$m_{DE} = \dfrac{3 - (-1)}{8 - (-4)} = \dfrac{1}{3}$, so $m_{BC} = \dfrac{1}{3}$.
BC passes through $F(0; 6)$: $y = \dfrac{1}{3}x + 6$.
C is the intersection of BC and AE: $\dfrac{1}{3}x + 6 = -\dfrac{4}{5}x + \dfrac{47}{5} \Rightarrow 5x + 90 = -12x + 141 \Rightarrow x = 3$; $y = 7$, so $C(3; 7)$.
Radius $= CE = \sqrt{(3 - 8)^2 + (7 - 3)^2} = \sqrt{41}$.
$(x - 3)^2 + (y - 7)^2 = 41$

subQuestions.label: 11(d)
subQuestions.questionText: Determine the coordinates of B.
subQuestions.memoText:
A, C and E are collinear (line AE) with AC = CE, so C is the midpoint of AE:
$\left(\dfrac{x_A + 8}{2}; \dfrac{y_A + 3}{2}\right) = (3; 7) \Rightarrow A(-2; 11)$.
B is the midpoint of AD: $B = \left(\dfrac{-2 + (-4)}{2}; \dfrac{11 + (-1)}{2}\right) = (-3; 5)$.

questions.title: Analytical Geometry — Two Circles & a Shaded Region

subQuestions.label: 12(a)
subQuestions.questionText:
A circle with centre A and a circle with centre B are tangent at point C. The circle with centre B is tangent to the $y$-axis, BC is parallel to the $y$-axis, and A, B and C are collinear. The equation of the circle with centre B is $x^2 + y^2 - 4(3x + 2y) = -16$.

Determine the equation of the tangent to the circle at C.
subQuestions.memoText:
$x^2 - 12x + 36 + y^2 - 8y + 16 = -16 + 36 + 16$
$(x - 6)^2 + (y - 4)^2 = 36$; centre $B(6; 4)$, radius 6.
Since BC is vertical and C lies on circle B directly below B: $C(6; -2)$.
The tangent at C is perpendicular to BC (vertical), so it is horizontal: $y = -2$.

subQuestions.label: 12(b)
subQuestions.questionText: If the shaded region has an area of $28\pi$ units$^2$, determine the equation of the circle with centre A.
subQuestions.memoText:
Shaded area $=$ (area of circle A) $-$ (area of circle B):
$28\pi = \pi r_A^2 - \pi(6)^2 \Rightarrow \pi r_A^2 = 64\pi \Rightarrow r_A = 8$.
A lies on the vertical line $x = 6$, and circle A also passes through $C(6; -2)$, so $A(6; -2 + 8) = A(6; 6)$.
$(x - 6)^2 + (y - 6)^2 = 64$

subQuestions.label: 13(a)
subQuestions.questionText:
O is the centre of the circle. CF is a tangent to the circle at C. BC = CD and AE = ED. AD and BC are produced to G.

Study the list of statements and reasons: $\hat{C}_1 = \hat{C}_2 = x$ (vertically opposite angles); $\hat{C}_1 = \hat{A}_2 = x$ (tan-chord theorem); $\hat{A}_2 + \hat{B} + \hat{C}_4 = 180°$ (interior angles of $\triangle$); $\hat{A}_2 = \hat{A}_1 = x$ (equal chords, equal angles in the same segment); $\hat{A}_2 + \hat{A}_1 + \hat{C}_4 + \hat{C}_5 = 180°$ (opposite angles of a cyclic quad); $\hat{C}_3 + \hat{C}_5 = 90°$ (tangent $\perp$ radius).

Enter the correct angle numbers on the diagram above so that the statements and reasons make sense.
subQuestions.memoText: Label $\hat{A}_1$ and $\hat{A}_2$ at vertex A, and $\hat{C}_1, \hat{C}_2, \hat{C}_3, \hat{C}_4, \hat{C}_5$ at vertex C, consistent with the given statements: $\hat{C}_1 = \hat{C}_2$ are the vertically opposite angles at the intersection of AG and BC; $\hat{C}_1 = \hat{A}_2$ (tan-chord); $\hat{C}_3 + \hat{C}_5 = 90°$ (radius $\perp$ tangent CF). Award marks per correctly placed angle number.

subQuestions.label: 13(b)
subQuestions.questionText: Prove that OEFC is a cyclic quadrilateral.
subQuestions.memoText:
$\hat{E}_1 = 90°$ (line from the centre bisects a chord — OE $\perp$ AD, since AE = ED).
$\hat{E}_1 = \hat{C}_3 + \hat{C}_5 = 90°$.
$\therefore$ OEFC is a cyclic quadrilateral (converse — exterior angle of a cyclic quad equals interior opposite; or opposite angles supplementary since $\hat{E}_1 + (\hat{C}_3 + \hat{C}_5)$ are supplementary using the reflex configuration).

subQuestions.label: 13(c)
subQuestions.questionText: If $G\hat{C}F = x$, prove that $CG^2 = AG \times FG$.
subQuestions.memoText:
In $\triangle$ACG and $\triangle$CFG:
$\hat{G}$ is common.
$\hat{C}_2 = \hat{A}_1$ (both $= x$).
$\hat{CFG} = \hat{ACG}$ (third angle).
$\therefore \triangle$ACG $\;|||\;$ $\triangle$CFG (AAA).
$\therefore \dfrac{AC}{CF} = \dfrac{CG}{FG} = \dfrac{AG}{CG}$ (similar triangles, sides in proportion).
From $\dfrac{CG}{FG} = \dfrac{AG}{CG}$: $CG^2 = AG \times FG$.

questions.title: Euclidean Geometry — Proportion, Area & Pyramid Volume

subQuestions.label: 14(a)
subQuestions.questionText:
$\triangle$PQR has TS // QR, with $PT = x$ cm, $TQ = 16$ cm, $PS = x + 6$ cm, $SR = 20$ cm and $\hat{P} = \theta$. The area of $\triangle$PTS is $258{,}96$ cm$^2$.

Determine the area of the trapezium TQRS.
subQuestions.memoText:
$\dfrac{x}{16} = \dfrac{x + 6}{20}$ (proportion theorem — TS // QR)
$20x = 16x + 96 \Rightarrow x = 24$ cm, so $PT = 24$, $PS = 30$, $PQ = 40$, $PR = 50$.
Area $\triangle$PTS $= \dfrac{1}{2}(24)(30)\sin\theta = 258{,}96 \Rightarrow \sin\theta = 0{,}7193 \Rightarrow \theta = 45{,}9994° \approx 46°$.
Area $\triangle$PQR $= \dfrac{1}{2}(40)(50)\sin 46° = 719{,}34$ cm$^2$.
Area TQRS $= 719{,}34 - 258{,}96 = 460{,}38$ cm$^2$.

subQuestions.label: 14(b)
subQuestions.questionText:
P is moved so that P is the apex of a trapezoidal pyramid with base TQRS, and $\triangle$PTS forms an angle of $60°$ with the base TQRS.

Determine the volume of the trapezoidal pyramid using $\text{Vol}_{\text{pyramid}} = \dfrac{1}{3} \times \text{area of base} \times H$.
subQuestions.memoText:
$TS^2 = (24)^2 + (30)^2 - 2(24)(30)\cos 46°$ (cosine rule in $\triangle$PTS) $\Rightarrow TS = 21{,}81$.
Area $\triangle$PTS $= \dfrac{1}{2}(21{,}81)(\perp h) = 258{,}96 \Rightarrow \perp h = 23{,}75$.
The plane PTS makes $60°$ with the base: $\sin 60° = \dfrac{H}{23{,}75} \Rightarrow H = 20{,}57$.
$\text{Vol} = \dfrac{1}{3}(460{,}38)(20{,}57) = 3\,156{,}67$ cm$^3$
